item.title: Car engulfed in flames on Grantham Road
item.description: A car is on fire on Grantham Road this morning, with flames appearing to have started from the rear of the vehicle. A video received by fijivillage shows thick black smoke and flames coming from the back of the car as passing motorists slowed down to watch the incident.
item.content:encoded:
A car is on fire on Grantham Road this morning, with flames appearing to have started from the rear of the vehicle.

A video received by fijivillage shows thick black smoke and flames coming from the back of the car as passing motorists slowed down to watch the incident.

A car has been engulfed by fire on Grantham Road.

The cause of the fire has not been confirmed.

Drivers travelling through the area are advised to drive with caution while emergency services respond.

Questions have been sent to Police, and more details will be provided as they become available.

A journey shaped by resilience, compassion and a commitment to serving others takes centre stage on this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, as Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran shares the experiences that have defined her life.

item.title: Former dental assistant finds success through home baking business
item.description: Leaving a stable job as a dental assistant to pursue her passion for baking was a leap of faith for Natasha Sivo, but she says it has given her the flexibility to support her family while building a successful business from home. The 29-year-old owner of Natasha's Investment told fijivillage News that she worked as a dental assistant for almost seven years while selling food packs on the side befo
item.content:encoded:
Leaving a stable job as a dental assistant to pursue her passion for baking was a leap of faith for Natasha Sivo, but she says it has given her the flexibility to support her family while building a successful business from home.

The 29-year-old owner of Natasha's Investment told fijivillage News that she worked as a dental assistant for almost seven years while selling food packs on the side before realising that the income from her side business was higher than what she earned in her regular job.

Sivo, who has family connections to Taveuni, Bua and Savusavu, says her business offers a wide range of products, including custom cakes, cupcakes, pastries, pies, brownies, food packs and barbecue packs.

She also runs pop-up stalls during market days and provides catering for weddings, birthdays, engagements and other special occasions.

While the business has continued to grow, Sivo says balancing work and family remains one of her biggest challenges.

She says being a full-time mother to three children requires careful time management, while sourcing baking ingredients can also be difficult.

She also says Fiji's hot climate presents challenges when decorating cakes, requiring her to use more expensive ingredients to maintain the quality of her products.

She adds that she mainly promotes her business through Facebook, Instagram and word-of-mouth recommendations from family, friends and satisfied customers.

Despite increasing competition, Sivo says she does not see other businesses as a threat.

She says competition motivates her to improve and grow.

When asked whether she regrets leaving her career as a dental assistant, Sivo says she has no regrets.

She admits some relatives questioned her decision to leave a secure job, but says starting her own business has allowed her to work flexibly and put food on the table.

She says rather than working a nine-to-five job and leaving her children in someone else's care, she now has the opportunity to raise them while earning an income.

While encouraging other women and aspiring entrepreneurs, Sivo says people should not be afraid to pursue their business dreams.

She says there is strong support available through government programmes and other financial institutions to help women entrepreneurs and other MSMEs succeed.

Sivo is urging aspiring business owners to formally register their businesses, become tax compliant and take advantage of training programmes that help them develop financial management skills and grow sustainable businesses.

Meanwhile, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) were celebrated for their contribution to Fiji's economy, with 252 businesses recognised by the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service for their commitment to business development, tax compliance and continuous learning during the celebration of MSME Day in Suva last week.

Among them, 39 MSMEs successfully completed a comprehensive three-year training and coaching programme, graduating as independent businesses that are fully compliant with tax and customs requirements.

The event also saw the launch of the MSME Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) guide and MSME Newsletter, two new FRCS resources aimed at making tax compliance and business management easier for small businesses across Fiji.

Speaking at the launch, FRCS Director of Taxation Momina Beg highlighted that FRCS recognised that to help Fiji grow, it could not remain in its offices enforcing rules but instead needed to become a partner to businesses.

Beg says th e new publications were developed after listening to the concerns of MSMEs, many of whom had questions about taxation and business obligations but struggled to find answers outside office hours.

She says the FAQ guide provides step-by-step information on registering a business, understanding tax obligations, filing tax returns, bookkeeping requirements, VAT registration, PAYE registration and income tax obligations.

She adds the newsletter will keep MSMEs informed on key guidelines, including information for produce suppliers and middlemen in local supply chains, while providing updates on business and tax matters.

item.title: Grace Home Shelter and Golden Age Home Lautoka residents receive support
item.description: Residents of the Grace Home Shelter and Golden Age Home Lautoka Shelter have received cash, clothing and essential items from staff of the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection as part of an outreach initiative to support vulnerable members of the community. The donations were made during visits led by the Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Justice and Acting Permanent Secretary f
item.content:encoded:
Residents of the Grace Home Shelter and Golden Age Home Lautoka Shelter have received cash, clothing and essential items from staff of the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection as part of an outreach initiative to support vulnerable members of the community.

The donations were made during visits led by the Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Justice and Acting Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Women, Selina Kuruleca, before the team attended the Super Rugby Women's Grand Final in Ba.

The initiative is part of the Ministry's commitment to supporting those in need and strengthening community care.

The Ministry says the donations were made possible through generous contributions from Ministry staff, who donated cash and clothing, as well as a contribution from Mark Halabe of Mark Apparel.

They say the items will benefit street dwellers who have recently been integrated into residential homes and shelters over the past few weeks, helping them rebuild their lives with dignity and hope.

The outreach also included a visit to Ministry staff member Gulnaaz Bi, whose family lost everything in a devastating house fire last month. Staff presented donations collected by colleagues to assist the family as they recover from the tragedy.

Kuruleca thanked Ministry staff and Halabe for their generosity, saying the initiative reflects the Ministry's values of compassion, solidarity and service.

She says the Ministry works every day to support vulnerable individuals and families, and it is heartening to see its own staff leading by example.

Kuruleca says whether it is supporting people experiencing homelessness or standing beside a colleague during a difficult time, these acts of kindness remind us that, together, we can make a meaningful difference in the lives of others.

The Ministry also acknowledged the dedicated staff and management of the Grace Home Shelter and Golden Age Home Lautoka Shelter for the care and support they continue to provide to residents as they work towards rebuilding their lives.

item.title: New $460,000 farm road improves market access for 200 Macuata farmers
item.description: More than 200 farmers in the districts of Dogotuki, Udu and Cikobia in Macuata will now have safer and more reliable access to markets following the completion of a new 10-kilometre farm road under the Government's Rural Outer Island Development Programme. The Nubunisoqosoqo Farm Road in Dogotuki, Macuata, was officially commissioned this week by the Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and
item.content:encoded:
More than 200 farmers in the districts of Dogotuki, Udu and Cikobia in Macuata will now have safer and more reliable access to markets following the completion of a new 10-kilometre farm road under the Government's Rural Outer Island Development Programme.

The Nubunisoqosoqo Farm Road in Dogotuki, Macuata, was officially commissioned this week by the Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Management, Mosese Bulitavu.

Built at a cost of more than $460,000 , the road was constructed in three phases under the Coalition Government's Rural Outer Island (ROI) Development Programme.

The project is expected to improve the transportation of agricultural produce to markets while making it easier for farmers to access essential farming supplies. It will also provide safer and more reliable access between farming areas and the main road network.

The new infrastructure is expected to encourage further agricultural investment and support the growth of small businesses in the area.

Bulitavu says t he project reflects the Government's commitment to providing rural communities with the infrastructure needed to improve livelihoods and stimulate economic growth.

He says roads such as the Nubunisoqosoqo Farm Road are pathways to opportunity, connecting farmers to markets, improving access to essential services and creating opportunities for economic growth in rural communities.

item.title: Former LDS missionary urges young Fijians to embrace agriculture as a business opportunity
item.description: Young Fijians should see agriculture as a pathway to business success rather than just farming, according to Utah businessman and former LDS missionary Blake Soifua, who says Fiji has the potential to become a global supplier of premium agricultural products if farmers have better access to overseas markets. Soifua says agriculture remains the backbone of the South Pacific and believes many young
item.content:encoded:
Young Fijians should see agriculture as a pathway to business success rather than just farming, according to Utah businessman and former LDS missionary Blake Soifua, who says Fiji has the potential to become a global supplier of premium agricultural products if farmers have better access to overseas markets.

Soifua says agriculture remains the backbone of the South Pacific and believes many young people in Fiji are surrounded by opportunities but do not always know how to take advantage of them.

Insert: Soifua on surrounded by opportunities 26th July 26

He is encouraging young people to work with their Turaga ni Koro and village leaders to access land and invest in farming, saying there is strong demand in the United States for quality Fijian produce.

Soifua says he has travelled across Fiji, visiting farming communities in Bua, Nadroga, Navosa, Naitasiri and Ba, where he spoke with farmers to better understand the challenges they face.

He says one of the biggest issues raised by farmers is finding reliable overseas markets and increasing exports.

According to Soifua, Fiji has the potential to build a global reputation for products such as turmeric, ginger and dalo, just as Fiji Water has become an internationally recognised brand.

R eflecting on his time serving an LDS mission in Fiji, Soifua says he encouraged families to become more self-reliant through farming so they could better meet everyday expenses, including transport costs, instead of depending on others.

H e also expressed concern over Fiji's association with drug trafficking following the seizure of 2,000 kilograms of cocaine in Ba, saying farming offers young people a far more sustainable and rewarding future than making quick money from illegal activities.

Soifua is also urging farmers to make better use of social media platforms, particularly TikTok, to promote their produce and connect with buyers overseas.

Drawing from his own experience as a business owner in Utah, he says marketing is essential because people cannot buy products they do not know exist.

item.title: Work to remove first three derelict vessels from Suva Harbour set to begin
item.description: The committee agreed to move ahead with the next phase of the clean-up under the Captain Johnathan Smith Fund, which aims to improve the condition of Suva Harbour. Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Prime Minister, Dr Lesikimacuata Korovavala, said careful planning had been undertaken to ensure the project was ready to progress.
item.content:encoded:
The committee agreed to move ahead with the next phase of the clean-up under the Captain Johnathan Smith Fund, which aims to improve the condition of Suva Harbour.

Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Prime Minister, Dr Lesikimacuata Korovavala, said careful planning had been undertaken to ensure the project was ready to progress.

He says the Captain Johnathan Smith Fund continues the legacy of the late Captain Johnathan Smith, with the goal of creating a cleaner and healthier Suva Harbour for future generations.

The meeting followed the finalisation of an operational agreement outlining how the clean-up will be managed by the Government, the Joint Maritime Environment Committee, Fiji Ports Corporation Limited, the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji, the Waitt Institute and Blue Prosperity Fiji.

Fiji Ports Corporation Limited will oversee all operational aspects of the vessel removal, including managing contractors responsible for cleaning and scuttling the vessels in line with Fiji's legal requirements.

The vessels will only be scuttled after meeting strict environmental and safety standards certified by the Department of Environment and the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji.

Permanent Secretary for Environment and Climate Change, Dr Sivendra Michael says removing derelict vessels from Suva Harbour demonstrates Fiji's commitment to protecting its marine environment and meeting its environmental and climate commitments.

He adds that the abandoned vessels have posed risks to traditional custodians, marine ecosystems, navigation and public safety for many years, and their removal will help restore the ecological integrity of the harbour.
